title: Choose the TradingAgents UI visual world
question: Keep the rolled dispatch world, choose the research docket, adopt a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Block Dispatch
options.lineage: railway train-graph dispatch sheets and illuminated block panels
options.thesis: Every analysis travels a governed line: evidence enters fixed blocks, handoffs clear, and the final signal leaves with a traceable route.
options.viewport: A four-column control desk launches into an eight-column live dispatch graph, with recent runs docked beneath both above the fold.
options.risk: The railway lineage becomes decoration unless every line and block maps directly to a real agent, handoff, or run state.

raised.raise: Disagreement is visible as intersecting Bull and Bear routes instead of a vague research status.
Running states show direction and progress before warnings appear.
Every message stays pinned to its producing stage and time.
Completed reports become persistent occupied blocks instead of evaporating feed items.
The analysis date remains a primary locator on every active and historical run.
Importance and terminal state use scale, labels, and shape rather than colour alone.

options.label: Research Docket
options.lineage: institutional research folders, indexed exhibits, and signed investment memoranda
options.thesis: Each run is an evidence docket assembled from analyst exhibits into one signed final memorandum.
options.viewport: The analysis form reads as a cover sheet beside an open evidence file, with recent dockets indexed along the bottom edge.
options.risk: It is familiar to research users, but its document density can underplay the energy and sequence of live agent work.

options.label: Exposure Sheets
options.lineage: darkroom exposure records on layered tracing sheets
options.thesis: Analyst outputs overlap as weighted evidence sheets, and crossed hatches expose unresolved conflicts.
options.viewport: Configuration sits on a fixed zone legend while report layers slide across one shared evidence field.
options.case: The conflict grammar is excellent, but darkroom notation identifies less strongly with TradingAgents users and obscures the fixed agent sequence.
options.kept: Make disagreement legible without depending on semantic colour.
options.risk: Dense hatching can compete with form labels and markdown reports.

options.label: Night Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six trusted instruments cross-check the run while needles reveal drift before a warning lamp fires.
options.viewport: Configuration and recent runs flank a fixed constellation of live agent instruments.
options.case: Instrument trust is strong, but round gauges imply independent metrics rather than a sequential collaborative analysis.
options.kept: Show trend and deviation before escalating to an alarm.
options.risk: The dark cockpit can collapse into the neon terminal cliché the direction round is meant to avoid.

options.label: Mesophotic Descent
options.lineage: a staged technical dive down a volcanic wall
options.thesis: The run descends through evidence layers, marking every observation before turning upward with a decision.
options.viewport: A vertical stage axis anchors live messages while configuration and reports open as pinned observations.
options.case: Depth maps progression clearly, but the descent narrative misstates a branching debate-and-handoff graph.
options.kept: Pin each observation to its exact stage and moment.
options.risk: Atmospheric depth can reduce contrast and make standard controls feel foreign.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: weather blocks cut and assembled in a cloud quarry
options.thesis: Agents cut transient evidence into durable report blocks before releasing a final signal.
options.viewport: A compact control tally faces a construction field where completed reports settle into a run structure.
options.case: Persistent blocks suit report completion, but the surreal quarry is weak audience identification and hides familiar analysis affordances.
options.kept: Completed work should gain visible permanence and weight.
options.risk: The metaphor can become playful spectacle in a serious operating surface.

options.label: Analysis Almanac
options.lineage: a printing-house wall calendar and tear-off date pad
options.thesis: The selected market date governs the run, and history accumulates as a tactile sequence of dated leaves.
options.viewport: A large date pad anchors configuration while active evidence and recent dated runs occupy the upper plate.
options.case: Date memory helps history, but it overstates scheduling and understates agents, reports, and the final decision.
options.kept: Keep the analysis date visible as a first-class locator.
options.risk: The vernacular calendar can read nostalgic and ornamental rather than operational.

options.label: Decision Atlas
options.lineage: a celestial atlas with ranked magnitudes and indexed plates
options.thesis: Agent observations form a coordinate field whose strongest evidence resolves into one named signal.
options.viewport: A plotted agent field dominates the workspace while controls and recent runs read as its indexed plates.
options.case: Ranked evidence is legible, but the atlas suggests exploratory data visualization rather than a deterministic run pipeline.
options.kept: Encode importance with scale and form as well as colour.
options.risk: Canvas spectacle can displace accessible controls and long-form report reading.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar SaaS dashboard for configuring runs, watching status cards, and opening reports.
canonCard.viewport: A top navigation bar sits above a form card, summary cards, and a recent-runs table.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but intentionally indistinguishable from competing developer dashboards.
